ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit diagram is a DC power supply labeled 10 V; the upper end of the power supply is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor at the top to the output node on the right. From this output node downward there are two parallel branches: one is the ideal Zener diode branch in the middle, and the other is the resistor branch on the right labeled 1 kΩ. The output voltage Vo is marked across the 1 kΩ resistor on the right, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative. Reasoning: According to the specified method, first assume that the Zener diode is cut off, equivalent to an open circuit. At this time the remaining circuit is just a 10 V power supply in series with two 1 kΩ resistors, and Vo is the voltage across the lower/right 1 kΩ resistor. By the voltage division formula, Vo = 10 × 1 kΩ / (1 kΩ + 1 kΩ) = 5 V. Then compare with the Zener voltage 6 V; 5 V < 6 V, therefore the Zener diode will not enter breakdown conduction, and the initial cutoff assumption is self-consistent. Therefore the output voltage is 5 V.

method.method_draft: Assume the Zener is regulating, so the output node would be clamped at 6 V. Then the current through the load resistor seen in the image would be 6 V / 1 kΩ = 6 mA. The current supplied through the series 1 kΩ resistor from the 10 V source would be (10 V − 6 V) / 1 kΩ = 4 mA. KCL would require the Zener current to be source current minus load current, 4 mA − 6 mA = −2 mA, which is impossible for a conducting Zener in this shunt configuration. Thus the Zener is off. With it off, the two 1 kΩ resistors form a simple divider from 10 V, giving Vo = 5 V.

claims.source: The Zener diode is cut off, equivalent to an open circuit

claims.claim: Under the assumption that the Zener diode is open-circuited, the remaining circuit is a 10 V power supply in series with two 1 kΩ resistors.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: At this time the remaining circuit is a 10 V power supply in series with two 1 kΩ resistors

claims.claim: Under the assumption that the Zener diode is open-circuited, Vo is the voltage on the lower or right-side 1 kΩ resistor.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Vo is the voltage on the lower/right-side 1 kΩ resistor

claims.claim: The voltage division formula can be used to find the voltage across a certain resistor in series resistors.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: From the voltage division formula

claims.claim: Using the voltage division formula gives Vo = 10 × 1 kΩ / (1 kΩ + 1 kΩ).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Vo = 10 × 1 kΩ / (1 kΩ + 1 kΩ)

claims.claim: The voltage division calculation result of Vo is 5 V.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Vo = 10 × 1 kΩ / (1 kΩ + 1 kΩ) = 5 V

claims.claim: The Zener voltage is 6 V.
claims.label: perception
claims.source: Zener voltage 6 V

claims.claim: 5 V is less than 6 V.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: 5 V < 6 V

claims.claim: Because 5 V is less than 6 V, the Zener diode will not enter breakdown conduction.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore the Zener diode will not enter breakdown conduction

claims.claim: The initial cutoff assumption is self-consistent.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The initial cutoff assumption is self-consistent

claims.claim: The output voltage is 5 V.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: So the output voltage is 5 V
